id: ml-08
title: Residual networks
paper: He, Zhang, Ren & Sun, Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition (arXiv Dec 2015; CVPR 2016)
link: https://arxiv.org/abs/1512.03385
type: Replication
cutoff: 2015-12-10
domain: ml
profile: method-benchmark

## expected_verdict
Supported (strong) as a positive control, with a weak adjudicator. The paper's own controlled comparison makes the causal case: plain vs residual nets at equal depth, with the degradation problem visible in training error. The listed adjudicator (Bag of Tricks) re-implements ResNet-50 and improves it, but never re-tests residual vs plain. It confirms reproducibility of ResNet, not the causal claim.

## I0
Do residual connections improve optimization and accuracy of deep image classifiers?

## evidence
- Degradation problem: deeper plain nets have higher training error (CIFAR-10 20 vs 56 layers, Fig. 1; ImageNet plain-18 vs plain-34, Fig. 4), so it is not overfitting.
- Controlled comparison (Table 2, ImageNet val top-1, 10-crop): plain-18 27.94 vs ResNet-18 27.88; plain-34 28.54 vs ResNet-34 25.03. Same depth, parameters and FLOPs (identity shortcuts add none).
- Depth scaling: ResNets up to 152 layers (8× deeper than VGG, lower complexity); ensemble 3.57% top-5 test error, ILSVRC 2015 winner; 28% relative improvement on COCO detection.
- CIFAR-10 analysis with 110 and 1202 layers (1202 overfits).
- Adjudicator content: He et al. 2018, Bag of Tricks (Amazon): ResNet-50 top-1 raised from 75.3% to 79.29% with training-procedure refinements; does not include plain-network controls.

## intake
- Scope: residual (identity-shortcut) connections ease optimization of deep nets and let accuracy improve with depth.
- Regime: ImageNet and CIFAR-10 CNNs, 18–152 layers (CIFAR up to 1202), SGD + BatchNorm.
- Assumptions: plain and residual nets differ only in shortcuts; training recipes are identical.
- Falsifiers: plain nets matched to ResNets with a better recipe (initialization, normalization) close the gap at the same depth; no training-error degradation for plain nets.

## screen
- Must flag: the gain is small at 18 layers and large at 34; later recipe improvements confound comparisons across papers.
- Must request: plain vs residual at matched recipe and depth in any replication.

## retrieval
- Pre-cutoff must-finds: Highway Networks (Srivastava et al. 2015); VGG; GoogLeNet; BatchNorm (Ioffe & Szegedy 2015); He et al. 2015 PReLU / MSRA initialization; vanishing gradients (Bengio et al. 1994).
- Current mode: Bag of Tricks (above): reproducibility of ResNet-50 and recipe effects; not a causal replication.

## designer
- Compare plain vs residual at depths 18 / 34 / 50 with an identical modern recipe; measure training curves and validation error; separate recipe tricks from architecture.

## champion
- Plain network of equal depth with the best available initialization and normalization (the strongest non-residual control).

## panel
- Accept; note the adjudicator's limitation and request an independent plain-vs-residual replication for tier assignment.

## run
- CIFAR-10: plain-20/56 vs ResNet-20/56 with identical recipe; reproduce higher training error for plain-56 and the residual advantage. A few GPU hours.

## verdict
- Label: Supported (strong) from the paper's controlled evidence and broad reproduction; independent causal replication not in inventory.
- Must say: depth-specific optimization benefit; a later stronger ResNet-50 recipe is not a causal replication.
- Must not say: Bag of Tricks confirms the residual mechanism; or residual connections are unnecessary.

## audit
- Check: Table 2 numbers (27.94/27.88; 28.54/25.03); 3.57%; 152 layers; Bag of Tricks 75.3 → 79.29.

## variants
- Test the residual contribution at new depths and matched modern recipes (e.g. plain nets with improved normalization).
